title: TESS 2-min light curves (2019-2026) show transit-duration trends in 6 of 120 planets around hot stars and 1 of 271 around cooler stars; WASP-167 b is a new nodal-precession candidate
abstract: Question: Do secular changes of transit duration (T14), which nodal precession around fast-rotating oblate stars causes, occur preferentially around hot stars in a uniform TESS sample? Does TESS show new precessing planets? Approach: We fit TESS SPOC 2-min PDCSAP light curves from sectors 1-107 (2018-2026, 2,620 files) for 419 confirmed planets with P < 10 d, depth >= 0.3 %, Tmag <= 12.5 and data in at least two seasons over at least 1.5 yr. In each season we fit a batman model: a/R* and limb darkening were shared, and Rp/R*, impact parameter and time offset were free. Each transit had its own linear baseline, delta-Scuti pulsations were prewhitened, and errors came from a bootstrap over transits. We calibrated the error scale on 134 cool hosts (Teff <= 5700 K). Results: 6 of 120 hot-host planets (Teff >= 6250 K) have T14 trends above 3 sigma, against 1 of 271 cooler-host planets (one-sided Fisher p = 0.004). Four of the five planets with published precession pass 3 sigma, and WASP-33 b has z = -3.0. For TOI-1518 b, the published rate predicts the 2024 durations out of sample (chi2 0.1 against 70.7 for no change). Our db/dt = -0.0119 +- 0.0009 /yr agrees with the published -0.0116 +- 0.0036 /yr. The KELT-9 b decrease agrees with the Doppler-tomography rate (chi2 4.4 for 3 dof, against 108.7 for no change). WASP-167 b, a retrograde planet of a rapidly rotating F1V star, is a new candidate: T14 increases monotonically from 176.7 to 181.9 min between 2019 and 2026 (+0.70 +- 0.10 min/yr, z = 6.7 over four seasons; z = 7.3 to 8.9 in other variants), so db/dt is approximately -0.0033 /yr. HAT-P-70 b, a near-polar planet of an A star, shows a weaker trend (z = 3.4 over two seasons). For 88 other hot-host planets with b > 0.3, the median 3-sigma limit on |db/dt| is 0.0057 /yr. Limitations: All results come from TESS alone. The model does not include gravity darkening or eccentricity, so absolute b values for fast rotators are biased. Many planets have only two seasons. Without the five known precessors, the population excess is not significant (2/115 against 1/271, p = 0.21).

display.caption: Calibrated significance of the TESS transit-duration trend against host effective temperature for 391 planets (left), and z histograms for cool and hot hosts (right). Points above |z| = 3 are labelled. Five of the six hot-host flags are known precessors or the new candidate WASP-167 b. The cool flag TOI-1811 b agrees with the chance expectation.

Positive controls. Black points: the measured T14 change from the first TESS season. Red: the change that the published db/dt predicts (TOI-1518 b: Watanabe et al. 2024; KOI-13 b: Szabo et al. 2020; WASP-33 b and KELT-9 b: Stephan et al. 2022; TOI-1355 b: discovery paper, same data). Error bars are the uncalibrated bootstrap errors (conservative by about 1.5 times).

Per-season T14 (top) and impact parameter (bottom) for the new candidate WASP-167 b, the weak candidate HAT-P-70 b, and the single cool-host flag TOI-1811 b. Red lines show the weighted linear trend. Titles give the slope with calibrated error and z. Error bars are the uncalibrated bootstrap errors.

citations.reason: We reuse its NASA Exoplanet Archive pscomppars transiting-planet snapshot (2026-11-08) for sample selection, because the archive was unavailable on 2026-11-09.
Related campaign TESS 2-min hot-Jupiter timing study (period changes). This work measures durations instead.
Stephan et al. 2022: WASP-33 b and KELT-9 b precession rates used as controls. Our TESS T14 decline of KELT-9 b supports a growing impact parameter (the Table 1 sign).
Watanabe et al. 2024 (PASJ 76, 374): TOI-1518 b db/dt from 2019 and 2022 data. Our 2024 TESS durations agree out of sample.
Szabo et al. 2020: Kepler-13A b db/dt used as a control.
TOI-1355 b discovery paper (PASJ 2026): db/dt from the same TESS sectors, used as an in-sample control.
Temple et al. 2017: discovery of WASP-167 b/KELT-13 b, with a retrograde orbit (lambda = -165 deg) around a rapidly rotating pulsating F1V star.
Bello-Arufe et al. 2022: HAT-P-70 b near-polar orbit and v sin i.
